title: Matched-surrogate tests flag geometry-only FC as pair-specific wiring in worm, fly, mouse and human calibrations; only fly and sedated-mouse wiring gains exceed the largest geometry-only gain
abstract: Question: earlier campaign studies compared the FC gain of real wiring with that of surrogate wiring with matched node strengths and distance law. What do these tests report when the source of FC is known? Method: for worm (40 animals), fly (48 flies; rest, walk), mouse (79 sedated, 10 isoflurane-only, 6 awake; one hemisphere) and human (69 persons) we made synthetic FC that keeps the observed node and distance structure and noise, and planted a signal from real wiring, surrogate wiring, mixtures or pure geometry. We ran the same cross-validated surrogate test (four definitions) on 451-766 synthetic data sets per condition. Results: without node terms (the earlier headline test), all planted signals gave overlapping surrogate shares, so the reported 48-100 % shares are not diagnostic. With node terms, planted surrogate wiring gave p <= 0.05 in at most 15 % of runs and planted real wiring was detected in 100 % at full amplitude. But geometry-only FC gave p <= 0.05 in 73-100 % of worm, 50-100 % of mouse, 0-70 % of human and 0-100 % of fly runs; a geometric base block did not remove this. At the observed gain level, power was 42-57 % in worm and 52-70 % in human. The observed direct + indirect wiring gain reached or exceeded the largest gain from geometry-only FC in fly (0.99-1.17x) and in mouse under medetomidine + isoflurane (1.14-1.60x), but not under isoflurane alone (0.52-0.82x), awake (0.44-0.70x), in worm (0.19-0.23x) or human (0.18x). With a geometric base block, fly (1.97x), mouse (2.73x) and worm (1.40x) exceeded the eigenmode ceiling; human (0.31x) did not. Thus the sedation effect in mouse survives calibration, and walking did not change the fly result. Limitations: two geometry families only; mouse iso and awake noise uses an assumed residual reliability; one mouse hemisphere; few replicates on an overloaded host; region-scale graphs; mouse and human wiring models are partly geometric.
